opts: An obstetric conjugate below 10 cm, or a diagonal conjugate below 11.5 cm
A true conjugate below 12 cm, which is the usual threshold applied
A bituberous diameter below 10 cm measured at the pelvic outlet
An interspinous diameter below 10 cm in the mid-cavity
exp: Clinical pelvimetry flags contraction when the obstetric conjugate is under 10 cm or the diagonal conjugate under 11.5 cm.

opts: Low-lying: type I — placenta previa: types I, II and III reaching or covering the os
Low-lying: types I to IV — placenta previa: type I alone
Low-lying: type II — placenta previa: types III and IV only
Low-lying: type I — placenta previa: type IV alone
exp: In the new classification low-lying placenta is type I, while placenta previa covers types I to III reaching or covering the os.

q: Vascular connections between twins — dichorionic : monochorionic diamniotic : monoamniotic.
opts: Dichorionic: none — monochorionic diamniotic: deep arteriovenous — monoamniotic: superficial
Dichorionic: deep arteriovenous — monochorionic diamniotic: none — monoamniotic: superficial
Dichorionic: superficial — monochorionic diamniotic: deep — monoamniotic: none at all
Absent in all three, since anastomoses do not follow chorionicity
exp: Dichorionic placentas have no connections; monochorionic diamniotic placentas have deep arteriovenous ones, and monoamniotic placentas superficial ones.

q: Match the uterine incision — Sanger's : Kerr's : Kronig's.
opts: Sanger's: classical upper segment vertical — Kerr's: lower segment transverse — Kronig's: low vertical
Sanger's: lower segment transverse — Kerr's: classical vertical — Kronig's: J-shaped
Sanger's: low vertical — Kerr's: classical upper segment — Kronig's: lower segment transverse
Sanger's: T-shaped extension — Kerr's: lower segment transverse — Kronig's: classical
exp: Sanger's is the classical vertical incision, Kerr's the standard lower segment transverse, and Kronig's a low vertical incision.

opts: Heart failure from left ventricular systolic dysfunction with an ejection fraction below 45% in the last month or first five months postpartum
Spontaneous coronary artery dissection presenting at 20 weeks of gestation
Aortic valve vegetations appearing during the first year after delivery
A congenital ventricular septal defect first detected in the third trimester
exp: Peripartum cardiomyopathy is defined by its timing, by systolic dysfunction and by the absence of another identifiable cause.

opts: Goodell's sign, softening of the cervix felt from about six weeks
Hegar's sign, softening of the lower uterine segment
Piskacek's sign, asymmetrical softening of the uterine cornu
Palmer's sign, rhythmic contraction of the uterus felt on examination
exp: Goodell's sign is the earliest probable sign on bimanual examination; Hegar's and Piskacek's follow a little later.

opts: No biophysical profile at all, since bile acid levels alone guide management
Weekly non-stress test and biophysical profile, with growth scans every three weeks
Daily ultrasound examination of the fetus and the placenta alone
A monthly non-stress test until the planned delivery
exp: Surveillance in cholestasis is intensified because of the stillbirth risk: weekly testing with growth scans every three weeks.

q: Match the bedside kit tests: the Actim test and the Amnisure test detect:
opts: Actim: placental protein 12, or insulin-like growth factor binding protein-1 — Amnisure: PAMG-1
Actim: PAMG-1 — Amnisure: alpha-fetoprotein in the vaginal fluid
Both tests detect human chorionic gonadotrophin in vaginal fluid
Both tests detect fetal fibronectin in cervicovaginal secretions
exp: Actim detects IGFBP-1 (placental protein 12) and Amnisure detects placental alpha microglobulin-1 in vaginal fluid.

opts: A newer, smaller, portable disposable vacuum device used for occipito-anterior and posterior positions
A metal cup designed for delivery of the face presentation
A rotational forceps with a sliding lock for the transverse head
A fetal scalp electrode used to monitor the heart rate in labour
exp: The Omnicup is a modern handheld vacuum device suitable for both occipito-anterior and occipito-posterior positions.

q: Interpretation of the Bishop score — 5 or less : 6 or more : 9 or more.
opts: 5 or less: unripe and induction likely to fail — 6 or more: favourable — 9 or more: like spontaneous labour
5 or less: favourable — 6 or more: unripe — 9 or more: induction has already failed
5 or less: unripe — 6 or more: still unripe — 9 or more: favourable for induction
5 or less: vaginal delivery certain — 6 or more: favourable — 9 or more: unripe
exp: A score of 5 or less predicts a failed induction, 6 or more is favourable, and 9 or more behaves like spontaneous labour.

opts: Term prelabour rupture only; not in early or late preterm rupture
Early preterm rupture of membranes only, to avoid ascending infection
Late preterm rupture of membranes only, once the lungs are mature
All three groups, since rupture of membranes alone is an indication
exp: Induction is listed only for term prelabour rupture; preterm rupture is managed expectantly unless another indication appears.

opts: Cord entanglement with sudden death of both twins; steroids and caesarean at 32-34 weeks
Twin-to-twin transfusion syndrome treated by laser ablation of the anastomoses
Preterm labour alone, managed with a cervical cerclage
No specific risk at all, so vaginal delivery at term is appropriate
exp: Monoamniotic twins risk cord entanglement and sudden loss, so steroids are given and delivery planned by caesarean at 32-34 weeks.

opts: A reactive NST has a very high negative predictive value; a non-reactive one has a false-positive rate near 50%
A non-reactive NST is completely specific for imminent fetal death
A reactive NST still carries a false-negative rate of about 50%
Both results carry an identical positive predictive value of 90%
exp: A reactive NST is excellent for ruling out compromise; a non-reactive trace is poorly predictive and needs further testing.

opts: A 16 F catheter in the endocervical canal with the bulb at the internal os, inflated with 30 mL saline
A 12 F catheter in the vagina with the bulb at the external os, inflated with 10 mL
A 20 F catheter passed into the uterine cavity and inflated with 60 mL
A 16 F catheter left in the posterior fornix and inflated with 50 mL
exp: The bulb sits at the internal os and is inflated with 30 mL, stretching the cervix and stimulating prostaglandin release.

opts: A previous episiotomy and repair in an earlier delivery
Rh-positive status with a previously affected infant
New paternity, or a long interpregnancy interval
Breastfeeding alone, through sustained prolactin release
exp: The 'first exposure to a new placenta' hypothesis explains why a new partner or a long gap between pregnancies raises risk.

opts: Bright red, recurrent and painless, with no precipitating factor and often a small warning bleed
Dark red and non-recurrent, with severe abdominal pain and a tender uterus
A blood-stained mucus discharge mixed with the cervical show of labour
A continuous dark trickle of blood with a rigid, tender uterus
exp: Previa bleeds bright and painlessly with no trigger; pain, darkness and tenderness point to abruption instead.

opts: After 7-10 days, from ischaemic necrosis of the bladder with constant dribbling of urine
Immediately after delivery, from a direct laceration of the bladder wall
After six weeks, from a low-grade infection of the bladder
Within 24 hours, from trauma caused by the urethral catheter
exp: Pressure necrosis declares itself a week or so later as continuous painless dribbling of urine per vaginam.

opts: Rh D isoimmunisation alone, which is the only listed cause
Maternal obesity alone, acting through an unexplained mechanism
Maternal hyperthyroidism alone, causing fetal tachycardia
Chromosomal anomalies, parvovirus B19 or TORCH infection, and fetal anaemia
exp: Non-immune hydrops has chromosomal, infective, haematological and cardiac causes; Rh disease is the immune category.

opts: Donor: anaemia with heart failure — recipient: polycythaemia with thrombosis and failure
Donor: polycythaemia with thrombosis — recipient: anaemia and heart failure
Both twins become anaemic from the unbalanced transfusion
Both twins become polycythaemic from the shared circulation
exp: The donor is volume depleted and anaemic; the recipient is volume loaded and polycythaemic, with thrombotic and cardiac complications.

opts: The anterior buttock; breech is the exception where the denominator does not lie behind the symphysis
The sacrum itself, with the denominator behind the symphysis as it is in vertex
The posterior buttock, with the sacrum pointing anteriorly
The feet, which is why a breech has no denominator at all
exp: In breech the anterior buttock lies behind the symphysis, and the sacrum as denominator is the exception to the general rule.

opts: Extend the monitoring for a further 20 minutes to allow for the fetal sleep cycle
Perform an immediate emergency caesarean delivery for fetal distress
Administer a high-dose oxytocin infusion to stress the fetus
Discharge her with reassurance and repeat the test next week
exp: A non-reactive trace is extended to 40 minutes first, because the fetus may simply be asleep.

opts: Primary within 24 hours of delivery; secondary from 24 hours to 12 weeks afterwards
Primary within 6 hours of delivery; secondary between 6 and 24 hours
Primary within 1 hour of delivery; secondary from 1 to 7 days
Primary within 48 hours of delivery; secondary from 2 to 6 weeks
exp: Primary PPH is within 24 hours of birth and secondary PPH runs from 24 hours to 12 weeks postpartum.

opts: Chorion laeve, which becomes the chorionic part of the fetal membranes
Chorion frondosum, where the villi persist and form the definitive placenta
The Nitabuch layer, where maternal and fetal tissues meet and mix
Decidua vera, the maternal lining away from the implantation site
exp: Villi regress over the abembryonic pole giving chorion laeve; opposite the implantation site they persist as chorion frondosum.

opts: Hyperglycaemia, which is why they are contraindicated in diabetes
Hypoglycaemia, which needs regular monitoring of blood glucose
Bradycardia, which limits the dose that can safely be given
Isolated hypokalaemia, with no other metabolic disturbance
exp: Beta-agonists cause tremor, tachycardia, hypotension, pulmonary oedema and hyperglycaemia, so they are avoided in diabetes.

opts: Dichorionic diamniotic, with a separate amnion and chorion for each twin
Monochorionic diamniotic, sharing a single placental mass
Monochorionic monoamniotic, with both fetuses in one sac
Dichorionic monoamniotic, a recognised though uncommon combination
exp: Dizygotic twins are always dichorionic diamniotic, since each comes from a separate ovum with its own membranes.

opts: The baby cannot be delivered despite good contractions and full dilatation, from obstruction in the passage
Failure of the cervix to dilate despite adequate oxytocin augmentation
A latent phase lasting more than 20 hours in a primigravida
Delayed delivery caused by contractions that are too weak
exp: Obstruction means mechanical blockage with adequate powers; weak contractions are inertia, not obstruction.

opts: Severe fetal anaemia from isoimmunisation, parvovirus or vasa previa, or acute severe hypoxia
A benign physiological quiet sleep cycle in a healthy fetus
The normal fetal response to a meal eaten by the mother
Simple head compression as the head enters the pelvic inlet
exp: A sinusoidal pattern is ominous and points to severe anaemia or acute hypoxia, never to a benign sleep cycle.

opts: Seen in multiparous women; oxytocin-driven contractions worse with suckling, settling by day 3
Seen in primiparous women; prostaglandin-driven, persisting for two weeks
Caused by retained placental fragments and needing uterine curettage
Caused by infected lochia and treated with a course of antibiotics
exp: After-pains are intermittent oxytocin-driven contractions, commoner in multiparas, aggravated by breastfeeding and settling by the third day.
